q.en: Who is Jeff Polcen, and where does he work?
q.zh: 杰夫·波尔森(Jeff Polcen)是谁？他在哪里工作？

options.en: A zoo director in California who manages the largest elephant house on the West Coast and visits Cleveland only on vacation
options.zh: 加利福尼亚州一家动物园的园长，管理着西海岸最大的象馆，只有度假时才来克利夫兰

options.en: A veterinarian at a pet hospital
options.zh: 一家宠物医院的兽医

options.en: A lead zookeeper at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo
options.zh: 克利夫兰都会公园动物园(Cleveland Metroparks Zoo)的一名首席饲养员

options.en: A farmer in Ohio
options.zh: 俄亥俄州的一位农场主

explain.en: The book says, 'Jeff Polcen is a lead zookeeper at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo,' interviewed by Kathie Lester.
explain.zh: 书里说：「杰夫·波尔森是克利夫兰都会公园动物园的一名首席饲养员」，接受凯西·莱斯特(Kathie Lester)的采访。

q.en: According to Jeff, what is the MOST important skill for a zookeeper?
q.zh: 在杰夫看来，动物园饲养员最重要的技能是什么？

options.en: Cooking special meals for the animals, measuring each portion down to the gram and tasting the recipe himself before serving it
options.zh: 给动物做特餐，把每一份都精确到克来称量，上桌前还亲自尝一口配方

options.en: Observation—watching the animals to figure out what is happening
options.zh: 观察力——看着动物、判断正在发生什么事

options.en: Running very fast
options.zh: 跑得很快

options.en: Taking photographs of visitors
options.zh: 给游客拍照

explain.en: Jeff says, 'Observation is the most important skill. You have to be able to look at a group of animals and figure out what's happening'—like sickness, a birth, or conflict.
explain.zh: 杰夫说：「观察力是最重要的技能。你必须能看着一群动物、判断正在发生什么」——比如生病、要生产，或不和。

q.en: How long had Jeff worked in the African animal area at the zoo?
q.zh: 杰夫在动物园的非洲动物区工作了多少年？

options.en: 5 years
options.zh: 5 年

options.en: 30 years, the full length of his career from his first day to retirement
options.zh: 30 年，从他上岗第一天到退休的整个职业生涯

options.en: 2 years
options.zh: 2 年

options.en: 17 years

explain.en: Jeff says he started at the Birds of the World building, 'later transferred to the African animal area, where I've been for 17 years.'
explain.zh: 杰夫说他从「世界鸟类馆」做起，「后来调到非洲动物区，在那里已经干了 17 年」。

q.en: About how much does a giraffe weigh, according to the book?
q.zh: 根据这本书，一只长颈鹿大约有多重？

options.en: 500 to 700 pounds
50 to 100 pounds
5,000 to 6,000 pounds, the weight a fully grown male reaches just before the dry season when food runs short
options.zh: 5,000 到 6,000 磅，是一头成年公长颈鹿在旱季来临、食物变少之前达到的体重

explain.en: Jeff says, 'A giraffe weighs 1,500 to 2,500 pounds (680 to 1,134 kilograms), depending on whether it's male or female.'
explain.zh: 杰夫说：「一只长颈鹿重 1,500 到 2,500 磅（680 到 1,134 公斤），取决于它是公是母。」

q.en: What are 'mixed species exhibits' at Jeff's zoo?
q.zh: 在杰夫工作的动物园里，「混种展示区」(mixed species exhibits) 是什么？

options.en: Exhibits that are completely underwater, where the keepers dive in with masks to feed the animals and check on the fish twice every day
options.zh: 完全在水下的展区，饲养员戴着面罩潜进去喂动物，每天还要检查两次鱼的情况

options.en: Exhibits that contain only one animal
options.zh: 只养一种动物的展区

options.en: Exhibits with fake model animals
options.zh: 摆放假动物模型的展区

options.en: Yards where birds and mammals that are safe together live in the same space
options.zh: 把能安全共处的鸟类和哺乳动物养在同一片场地里的展区

explain.en: Jeff says, 'We run mixed species exhibits, where we have birds and mammals that are safe together in the same yard.'
explain.zh: 杰夫说：「我们经营混种展示区，把能安全共处的鸟类和哺乳动物放在同一片场地里。」

q.en: In the book, what does zoo 'furniture' mean?
q.zh: 在书中，动物园的「furniture」（家具）指的是什么？

options.en: Real chairs and tables for the keepers to rest on during their long night shifts, which often last until the animals wake at dawn
options.zh: 给饲养员在漫长久班中歇息用的真椅子和桌子，那些班常常要值到动物在黎明醒来

options.en: Vending machines for visitors
options.zh: 给游客用的自动售货机

options.en: Beds where the zookeepers sleep
options.zh: 饲养员睡觉的床

options.en: Natural objects like rocks and logs added to exhibits for the animals
options.zh: 添加到展区里、给动物用的自然物件，比如石头和原木

explain.en: Jeff says exhibit yards 'include what we call "furniture," like rocks and logs' to let animals show natural behaviors and avoid boredom.
explain.zh: 杰夫说展区里「有我们所谓的『家具』，比如石头和原木」，好让动物表现出自然行为、不至于无聊。

q.en: How does Jeff manage a group of giraffes?
q.zh: 杰夫是怎样管理一群长颈鹿的？

options.en: He separates every giraffe from the others, locking each one alone in a different barn at night so they cannot see or hear their herd mates until the sun rises, when he walks them out one by one to the empty yard for their morning check
options.zh: 他把每只长颈鹿都分开单独关，夜里把每一只锁在不同的畜棚里，让它们直到太阳升起都看不到、也听不见自己的伙伴；日出后他才一只接一只地把它们牵到空场地，做早晨的检查

options.en: He uses loud music to move them
options.zh: 他用很吵的音乐来驱赶它们

options.en: He trains them using only food treats
options.zh: 他只用食物奖励来训练它们

options.en: As herd animals, they follow a set routine; he uses his voice and sometimes a long stick to keep a safe distance
options.zh: 它们是群居动物，会遵循固定的流程；他用声音指挥，有时用长棍保持安全距离

explain.en: Jeff explains hoofed stock 'do everything as a group' and follow a routine. 'We give orders with our voices, and sometimes we'll use a long stick to tap them; it lets us keep a safe distance.'
explain.zh: 杰夫解释，有蹄动物「做什么都成群结队」、会遵循固定流程。「我们用声音下命令，有时用长棍轻点它们；这样能保持安全距离。」

q.en: Why does Jeff prefer mother-reared animals over hand-raised ones?
q.zh: 为什么杰夫更喜欢由母兽带大的动物，而不是人工喂养大的？

options.en: Because the mothers do not care for their young
options.zh: 因为母兽根本不照顾幼崽

options.en: Because hand-raised animals are dangerous to humans, having bitten several keepers at the zoo, which is why Jeff keeps them far from the public, wears thick gloves whenever he enters their pen, and trains them only through the bars of the cage
options.zh: 因为人工喂养的动物对人类很危险，已经咬过动物园里好几名饲养员，所以杰夫把它们远远隔开、不靠近公众，只要进栏就戴上厚手套，而且只在笼栏外训练它们

options.en: Because mother-reared animals learn to behave like their own species, while hand-raised ones may forget
options.zh: 因为由母兽带大的动物会学会像自己的同类那样行事，而人工喂养的可能会忘了

options.en: Because mother-reared animals are cheaper to keep
options.zh: 因为由母兽带大的饲养成本更低

explain.en: Jeff says, 'The mother-reared animal is better because it knows how to behave like the animal it is. Animals that are human-oriented forget to act like a zebra or a giraffe.' They only hand-raise if absolutely necessary.
explain.zh: 杰夫说：「由母兽带大的更好，因为它知道自己该怎样像同类那样行事。被人类带大的动物会忘了怎么像斑马或长颈鹿。」只有在万不得已时才人工喂养。

q.en: Why does the author present this book as an interview with Jeff Polcen?
q.zh: 作者为什么要把这本书写成对杰夫·波尔森的采访？

options.en: To let a real zookeeper share his firsthand experiences and expertise with readers
options.zh: 为了让一位真实的饲养员向读者讲述他的亲身经历与专业知识

options.en: To teach readers how to draw animals, with a step-by-step sketch of a giraffe at the end of every chapter and a list of art supplies to buy
options.zh: 为了教读者画动物，每一章末尾都有一幅长颈鹿的分步素描，还列了一份要买的画材清单

options.en: To tell a made-up fictional story
options.zh: 为了编一个虚构的故事

options.en: To sell tickets to the zoo
options.zh: 为了推销动物园门票

explain.en: The book is 'An Interview with Jeff Polcen / Conducted by Kathie Lester.' Presenting it as an interview lets the expert's real voice and experience teach readers about the job.
explain.zh: 这本书是「对杰夫·波尔森的采访／由凯西·莱斯特进行」。以采访形式呈现，能让专家真实的声音和经验来向读者介绍这份工作。

q.en: How does Jeff feel about his job as a zookeeper?
q.zh: 杰夫对自己饲养员的工作感受如何？

options.en: He is bored and wants to quit
options.zh: 他觉得无聊，想辞职

options.en: He thinks the job is much too easy
options.zh: 他觉得这工作太简单了

options.en: He dislikes the animals he cares for and counts the hours until each shift ends, often asking the director to give his yard to someone else so he can move to an office job far away from the smells, the noise, and the early morning feeds
options.zh: 他不喜欢自己照料的动物，数着时间盼每个班快点结束，还常请园长把他的场地分给别人，好让自己调去坐办公室，远离那些气味、喧闹和清晨的喂食

options.en: He finds it satisfying, interesting, and challenging, and wants to stay for the rest of his working life
options.zh: 他觉得这份工作令人满足、有趣又充满挑战，并想干上一辈子

explain.en: Jeff says, 'I would say so' about staying. 'I find caring for these animals very satisfying, interesting, and challenging,' with 'a lot I want to accomplish.'
explain.zh: 杰夫对是否留任说「可以这么说」。他「觉得照料这些动物非常满足、有趣又充满挑战」，还有「很多想完成的事」。

prompt.en: Jeff says observation is the most important skill and that every animal has its own personality. Think of an animal you know—a pet, a farm animal, or one at a zoo. What have you observed about how it behaves or what it needs? Why is careful observation important when caring for living things?
prompt.zh: 杰夫说观察力是最重要的技能，而且每只动物都有自己的个性。想一想你熟悉的一种动物——宠物、农场动物，或动物园里的。你观察到它怎样行为、需要什么？为什么在照料生命时，仔细的观察很重要？

en: Jeff says 'Observation is the most important skill' to notice sickness, birth, or conflict in a group (p. 4).
He notes 'All the animals have different personalities' and that is where observational skills help keepers safe (p. 14).
A good answer describes a real animal you have watched and explains why paying attention to its behavior matters.
zh: 杰夫说「观察力是最重要的技能」，用来察觉群体的生病、生产或不和（第4页）。
他指出「每只动物的个性都不同」，而观察力正是让饲养员保持安全的关键（第14页）。
好的回答要描述一种你真实观察过的动物，并说明留意它的行为为什么重要。
